text: The fatal night: Julia appears at the opening, swaying, by the light of the corridor-lamp
why: ¶50 says Julia appeared at the opening by the corridor-lamp, swaying.

text: The fatal night: Julia falls to the ground, convulsed
why: ¶50 says Julia's knees gave way, she fell, and her limbs were convulsed.

text: The fatal night: Julia shrieks out about a speckled band
why: ¶50 has Julia shriek out about the speckled band.

text: The fatal night: Julia stabs her finger towards the Doctor's room, and a convulsion chokes her words
why: ¶50 says Julia stabbed her finger toward the Doctor's room, and a convulsion choked her words.

text: The fatal night: Helen rushes out, calling for her stepfather
why: ¶50 says Helen rushed out calling loudly for her stepfather.

text: The fatal night: Helen meets Dr. Roylott hastening from his room in his dressing-gown
why: ¶50 says Helen met the Doctor hastening from his room in his dressing-gown.

text: The fatal night: Dr. Roylott reaches Julia, who is unconscious
why: ¶50 says that when the Doctor reached Julia she was unconscious.

text: The fatal night: Dr. Roylott pours brandy down Julia's throat
why: ¶50 says the Doctor poured brandy down her throat.

text: The fatal night: Dr. Roylott sends for medical aid from the village
why: ¶50 says the Doctor sent for medical aid from the village.

text: That morning: Helen tells how her sister died
why: Helen is speaking to Holmes this morning and recounts the death in ¶50.

text: Why has Helen Stoner come to Holmes now, two years after her sister's death? — she has met the same signs her sister met
id: q.why_helen_now=she has met the same signs her sister met
why: The story never says Helen has herself met the same signs her sister met; her reason for coming now is only vaguely described as fear and strain.

text: What was the speckled band that Julia cried out about?
why: A plain question raised by Julia's dying words in ¶50.

text: What was the speckled band that Julia cried out about? — a strip of cloth, such as a ribbon, strap or headcloth
id: q.what_band=a strip of cloth, such as a ribbon, strap or headcloth
why: The word 'band' gives a reader reason to consider a strip of cloth as one possibility.

text: What was the speckled band that Julia cried out about? — something living, marked with spots or bands
id: q.what_band=something living, marked with spots or bands
why: 'Speckled' plus the cheetah and baboon kept by the Doctor (¶27) give a reader reason to consider a living thing.

text: What was the whistle for? — a signal that the thing was done
id: q.whistle_for=a signal that the thing was done
why: The whistle is heard in ¶36–50 and is unexplained, so a signal is a reasonable possibility to consider.

text: What made the clanging sound?
why: A plain question raised by the clanging sound in ¶50.

text: What made the clanging sound? — something metal falling in Julia's room
id: q.clang=something metal falling in Julia's room
why: ¶50 says a mass of metal seemed to fall, and Julia's room is where the clanging was heard from the corridor.

text: What made the clanging sound? — something metal in Dr. Roylott's room
id: q.clang=something metal in Dr. Roylott's room
why: The metal sound is unlocated, and Julia's pointing toward the Doctor's room in ¶50 gives reason to consider that room.

text: At what hour did Julia scream?
why: A plain question; the story has given the whistle's three-o'clock timing as a reference point.

text: At what hour did Julia scream? — about three in the morning
why: ¶40 says Julia heard the whistle about three in the morning on previous nights, so this timing is a reasonable possibility.

text: At what hour did Julia scream? — well before three, not long after she locked her door
id: q.when_scream=well before three, not long after she locked her door
why: Julia locked her door after 11 o'clock (¶35–44) and the scream came later in the night, so an earlier time is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.

text: Who unlocked Julia's door?
why: A plain question raised by the door being unlocked and swinging open in ¶50.

text: What did Julia mean by pointing towards the Doctor's room?
why: A plain question raised by Julia pointing toward the Doctor's room in ¶50.

text: What did Julia mean by pointing towards the Doctor's room? — to accuse her stepfather
why: Julia pointed at the Doctor's room, so accusing him is a possibility the story gives reason to consider.

text: What did Julia mean by pointing towards the Doctor's room? — to show where the thing had come from
id: q.julia_pointed=to show where the thing had come from
why: Julia pointed toward the Doctor's room, so showing where the thing came from is a reasonable possibility.

text: What did Julia mean by pointing towards the Doctor's room? — to ask for the Doctor's help
id: q.julia_pointed=to ask for the Doctor's help
why: Pointing toward the Doctor's room while in distress makes asking for his help a reasonable possibility.

text: What did Julia mean by pointing towards the Doctor's room? — she meant nothing: it was part of the convulsion
id: q.julia_pointed=she meant nothing: it was part of the convulsion
why: Julia's words were cut off by convulsion, but the story also says she 'would fain have said' something, so 'meant nothing' is a possibility the reader can consider.

text: Was Dr. Roylott in his room when Julia screamed?
why: A plain question; the story says the Doctor had retired to his room early and only came out after Helen called.

text: Did anyone bring about Julia's death, and if so who? — as she was dying she pointed in the direction of the Doctor's room
why: The fact stated (she pointed toward the Doctor's room while dying) is in ¶50, and the question is neutrally worded.

text: What was the whistle for? — on the fatal night Helen seemed to hear it only after Julia had screamed
why: ¶50 says Helen heard the whistle only after she ran out following the scream.

text: What was the speckled band that Julia cried out about? — she pointed towards the Doctor's room
why: ¶50 states Julia pointed toward the Doctor's room while naming the speckled band.

text: How did Julia die? — she was chatting about her wedding that evening, and later came a sudden scream
why: ¶35 says Julia was chatting about her wedding that night, and ¶50 describes a sudden scream afterward.

text: How did Julia die? — she writhed in terrible pain and her limbs were dreadfully convulsed
why: ¶50 says she writhed as one in terrible pain and her limbs were dreadfully convulsed.
